# paper/model.tex vs implementation — line-by-line audit (2026-09-07)
<!-- Generated by Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic) -->
Sources read: postprocess/model_improved_pg.py (identify_executors/entities/callbacks, attribute_aspects,
_attribute_via_runtime, attach_callback_groups, detect_oort_threads, detect_joins, detect_state_links,
detect_polled_subs, mark_phases, split_callbacks, create_graph, add_horizontal_edges), gpu_dag.py
(build_typed_dag, classify_phases), gpu_dag_pg.py, fish_viz_server.py (_serve_task_graphs, _component_graph,
_namespace_views), wcc_dag_viz.py. Numbers checked on session fish_20260906_151532 (AW lean nsys_1).

## A. Statements in model.tex that do NOT match the code

1. Vertex tuple has no ns_v. FishVertex = (t_v, id_v, A_v, Z_v, level). Namespaces exist only as N.full_name
   and are derived on the fly by the viz (_namespace_views / _component_graph). Executor namespace sets are
   never computed. → say ns_v is derived from the node name, or drop it from the tuple.
2. Level-0 vertex. Code: CN ("container", label = session name, level −1) above EX (level 0). No hostname
   attribute on it (hostname lives in the sessions/hosts tables). Paper: H with A_v=(hostname), layers 0..4.
   → A_v(H) = (container id); index shift is cosmetic.
3. EX = a process (every vpid that fired rcl_node_init), not an executor object. A_v: pid, label
   "procname (PID)", executor_type + num_threads of the PRIMARY executor (the one owning most callback
   groups), extra_executors for processes with several executors, cb_groups. Paper: (pid, mode∈{ST,MT},
   threads). AW session: 70 SingleThreaded/1, 18 MultiThreaded/14. → "process with its primary executor's
   type and thread count".
4. E.etype set is {sub, serv, tmr, cli, waitable, oore}; external boundary entities are etype "sub" with
   external=true (not a kind). Paper: {tmr, sub, serv, cli, wait}. AW: 1443 sub, 1213 serv, 1007 cli,
   154 tmr, 7 oore. → add oore; state that ext is a flag.
5. F.ptype ∈ {cpu, oort, ext}; paper omits ext. F.phase ∈ {data, init, zero_exec, unknown} (AW: 2237 /
   93 / 1495 / 0) and oort F carry NO phase (7 None: detect_oort_threads runs after mark_phases).
   Paper: phase ∈ {init, data}. → list all four (zero_exec = registered but never fired, unknown = no
   periodic timer anywhere).
6. Phase rule is not "one-shot vs recurring". Code: per executor, data_phase_start = first fire of its
   earliest periodic timer (≥2 fires), session-level fallback; F is data iff ANY fire ≥ that boundary,
   init iff all fires precede it. A one-shot callback firing after the boundary is "data".
7. Partition claim is violated by the external boundary: ext E/F pairs have no parent node (AW: 381 E
   without a containing N). oort entities are attached to the FIRST node of their process (arbitrary).
8. Edge extraction direction. Code extracts msg/dep at the ENTITY level (L2) from entity aspects, pushes
   them DOWN to F (main F × main F; response edges to the client continuation F), then aggregates UP
   L2→L1 (node pairs) and L1→L0 (executor pairs). join, state and polled edges exist ONLY at L3 and are
   never lifted; gxf_internal is intra-node so it never reaches L1/L0. Paper: "extracted once at G4 and
   lifted with π". Equivalent for msg/dep only because every entity has exactly one main F.
   → "extracted at the entity–callback level and aggregated upward; join and state edges live only in G4".
9. dep edges are a request/response PAIR (direction attr), response to the client continuation F when
   split_callbacks ran. Paper gives only the request direction. Also observed: the request edge targets
   both the server entity (serv) AND the client entity of the same service (cli), because identify_entities
   gives client entities a (sub, service) aspect that puts them into srv_index (AW: 19 of 30 request
   edges end at a cli entity). Implementation quirk worth a decision, not a paper claim.
10. ext is not an edge type. Code: nature=msg with external=true, ext E (etype sub, external) + ext F
    (ptype ext, phase data). Paper's T includes ext. → either "ext edges" = msg edges with the external
    flag, or drop ext from T.
11. state has an OBSERVED variant: detect_polled_subs marks (s,p) polled=true, inferred=false when an
    rmw_take of s's topic happens inside p's callback window (Autoware InterProcessPollingSubscriber).
    Paper says every state edge is inferred. Also S requires: fired, data topic, no DATA pub aspect (may
    publish /diagnostics), not a join member; P = entities with a data pub aspect (any etype).
12. join membership includes non-completing subs of the same message type and timeout timers; ties are a
    star to the first completer (nature=join, intra_node). Paper's "two or more subscription callbacks…
    publish the same data topic" is the trigger; membership is wider.
13. memset is an SM node, not CE (Volta+ fill kernels; gpu_dag.build_typed_dag). Paper: "copies or memsets
    (ce)". CE = memcpy only.
14. GPU phase labels are INIT, WARMUP, STEADY, TAIL, COALESCED(N), UNKNOWN; paper lists three. Per-engine
    busy times C_cpu/C_sm/C_ce are NOT stored by the extractor; nodes carry c_min/c_max per node and the
    sums are derived downstream (gallery). Known bias: per-frame cudaMalloc pushes a steady shape to
    UNKNOWN (notes/campaign_split_v6_incidents.md).
15. Tasks. The implemented decomposition (fish_viz_server._serve_task_graphs) takes WCCs over ALL comm
    edges between F with a cb_addr (join and state included, no phase filter, no infra-topic filter, ext
    and oort F excluded because cb_addr='NA'), stripping only /parameter_events, /rosout and
    /_supported_types entities. wcc_dag_viz.py filters F by phase=data and, since 2026-09-06, drops infra
    topics/state edges/tooling nodes with --data-only. The paper's definition matches wcc_dag_viz --data-only,
    not the server route. → make the server route apply the same rule (or state the rule as implemented).
16. Namespace grouping. Code groups F/nodes by namespace prefix depth (ros axis, ns_depth 1..3); executors
    are grouped on a separate OS axis by EX vertex. "Depth-one prefix groups the executors serving it" is
    the old draft's Gr¹ and is not implemented. → "groups nodes (with their entities and callbacks) below
    the prefix; executors form a separate OS-axis grouping".
17. Aspects come from link events when present, else from a runtime window scan (rcl_publish /
    client_request_sent inside callback windows, first-active-callback fallback across threads); sub
    aspects come from `ros2 node info` + trace fallback, not from callbacks. Paper: "recovered from the
    link events" — true for the traced runs used in the paper; the fallback exists.
18. Hop latencies exist only when per-instance events were enabled (rmw_take / ipc_time); Isaac campaigns
    ran without them. Paper: "every message edge carries the observed hop latencies" → "when recorded".

## B. Statements that match
Hierarchy H/CN→EX→N→E→F with containment edges; Z sets; entity kinds' five dispatch paths; aspects on
entities (pub/sub/cli); msg rule pub(f)×sub(T) incl. same-node pairs (intra_node); delivery (ipc/dds/both)
as an attribute of the receiving F; join trigger rule; state S×P rule (with the refinements above); gxf
cross-product inside a NITROS I/O group; ext source/sink construction; invocation = callback window with
CUDA runtime calls (cb anchors) or gap-separated period (tid anchors); typed DAG nodes/edges launch,
cpu_order, stream_fifo; shapes by node-sequence signature; oort F anchored on thread.

## C. Suggested minimal edits to model.tex
- A_v(H): (container). EX: (pid, executor type, threads) "of the process's primary executor".
- etype: {tmr, sub, serv, cli, wait, oore}; ptype: {cpu, oort, ext}; phase: {data, init, zero_exec, unknown}.
- Phase sentence: "data if it fired after the executor's first periodic timer fired, init otherwise".
- Partition: "partition V_{ℓ+1} (external boundary vertices excepted)".
- Lifting sentence: "interaction edges are established between entities and their callbacks and aggregated
  upward; join and state edges exist only in G_4".
- dep: "a request edge f→g and a response edge g→f′ to f's continuation".
- state: "inferred unless an rmw_take of s's topic is observed inside p's execution window (polled)".
- ce: "copies (ce); memsets run as fill kernels on the SMs".
- GPU phases: "labelled init, warm-up, steady, tail or coalesced from their API signature".
- Tasks: keep the definition, and make _serve_task_graphs apply it (code change), or cite wcc_dag_viz.
- Namespace grouping: nodes/entities/callbacks by prefix; executors on the OS axis.
